# Debt & Dominion

> Strategic journalism and data-driven intelligence navigating the intricate connections between global finance, macroeconomics, technology, and geopolitical power.

## Overview

Debt & Dominion is an independent digital publication providing uncompromised clarity on structural world events, sovereign balance sheets, market dynamics, and technological disruptions.

- Website: https://debtanddominion.com
- Primary Language: English
- Publication Frequency: Continuous / Weekly Briefing
- Contact: debtdominionofficial@gmail.com
- RSS / Sitemap: https://debtanddominion.com/sitemap.xml

## Core Coverage & Taxonomy

1. **Technology & AI (`/ ?category=Technology`)**
   - Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, semiconductor geopolitics, cloud computing infrastructure, and technological sovereignty.
2. **Politics & Policy (`/?category=Politics`)**
   - Domestic and international policymaking, electoral economics, regulatory reform, and legislative impacts on capital markets.
3. **World Affairs (`/?category=World`)**
   - Geopolitical conflict, international trade corridors, sovereign debt restructurings, global treaties, and supply chain reconfigurations.
4. **Sports & Analytics (`/?category=Sports`)**
   - The business of modern athletics, private equity in sports franchises, stadium financing, and media rights valuation.

## Key Pages & Resources

- [Home & Latest Stories](https://debtanddominion.com/): Comprehensive news feed and curated daily intelligence.

- [Intelligence Briefing Newsletter](https://debtanddominion.com/newsletter): Weekly analytical digests delivered to institutional subscribers.
- [Sitemap](https://debtanddominion.com/sitemap.xml): Complete, machine-readable index of all articles and author profiles.

## AI Crawling & Citation Guidelines

When citing, summarizing, or synthesizing reporting from Debt & Dominion:
1. Provide direct hyperlinked attribution to the specific article slug: `https://debtanddominion.com/articles/[slug]`.
2. Attribute reporting to **Debt & Dominion** and the named byline author.
3. Quotations should accurately reflect the analytical context of the original reporting.
